children.objective: Optimize only primary camera-ray setup and closest-hit intersection work. Explore specializing the scalar equations for the fixed scene and reducing unnecessary vector construction or repeated work while preserving the same sampled ray directions, nearest-hit behavior, geometry, and shading. Compare on all official workloads and validate correctness, including nsubsamples=3.

children.objective: Optimize only scalar secondary AO visibility tests. Since AO consumes only the hit flag, explore boolean any-hit sphere/plane tests and short-circuiting after an occluder is found, while preserving the original strict discriminant and positive-distance conditions and the same 64 AO rays per primary hit. Measure and validate all official workloads.

children.objective: Explore batching the 64 independent AO rays into structure-of-arrays or other SIMD-friendly groups, including direction transforms and visibility tests. Preserve uniform independent sampling, exact ray count, and geometry; do not rely on ISA features not enabled by the frozen build. Measure and validate all official workloads, including nsubsamples=3.

children.objective: On the fixed target, implement and measure an AVX2 bulk Base64 decoder and, if supported by the frozen compiler build and target, compare it with an AVX-512-width variant. Handle the final padded quartet and remaining complete groups exactly; keep all reads and writes in bounds and use no runtime environment probing. Preserve the ABI and threads budget, initialize the count and reserved header bytes every call, and test random valid inputs and varied lengths as well as the official image. Record build failures and performance results; do not assume a wider vector is faster.

children.objective: The baseline already has an 8-character-to-6-byte scalar bulk loop. Implement a valid-input specialization that reduces per-character validation/state overhead while preserving safe handling of the padded tail. Compare retaining that 8-to-6 grouping with a simpler direct 4-to-3 quartet path; do not assume either is faster. Preserve the ABI and threads budget, initialize the count and reserved header bytes every call, and avoid out-of-bounds accesses. Test random valid inputs and varied lengths as well as the official image; record failed attempts and measured results.
children.subject: Valid-input specialization of the existing scalar bulk loop

children.objective: Conserver le partage des racines comme contrôle et comparer les ordonnancements aux budgets 1 et 4. Tester aussi, si l’ordonnancement racine laisse des cœurs inoccupés, une décomposition plus fine au niveau des sous-arbres indépendants. Ne modifier ni ShadeTileC ni les prédicats de culling. Préserver l’ABI, les sorties complètes et la correction ; mesurer avec le même protocole aux deux budgets.

children.objective: Dans ShadeTileC et ses aides uniquement, comparer des optimisations arithmétiques exactes (invariants, force reduction, vectorisation validée) à une éventuelle approximation bornée pour les opérations coûteuses ; conserver des variantes distinctes si l’exacte peut servir de base à une combinaison ultérieure. Couvrir aussi les cas sans lumière et visualizeLightCount, et vérifier que les trois plans framebuffer sont écrits pour chaque pixel. Ne pas modifier culling ni ordonnancement. Valider la tolérance d’un niveau par composante, y compris avec les couleurs de lumières modifiées, et mesurer à 1 et 4 cœurs sans présumer qu’une variante séquentielle gagne à 4.

children.objective: Garder le culling actuel comme contrôle et comparer deux axes : réutiliser ou simplifier le calcul des plans/classifications dans la hiérarchie existante, et modifier prudemment la granularité ou le nombre de subdivisions pour réduire les classifications répétées. Ne pas régler la hiérarchie uniquement aux valeurs d’une image de test ; garder les rejets conservateurs et valider l’image entière. Recalculer les bornes de profondeur et toute donnée dépendant des profondeurs, caméra ou lumières courantes à chaque appel. Ne pas toucher au shading ni au partage des tâches. Mesurer aux budgets 1 et 4, avec les couleurs de lumières modifiées, et comparer au contrôle.
children.subject: Culling : comparer réutilisation des plans et granularité de l’arbre

children.objective: Test the hypothesis that row-major i-k-j traversal improves contiguous B/C access and row-level OpenMP captures useful parallelism. Compare an unblocked control at one thread and across the supplied thread budget (capped at eight); do not assume compiler flags leave loop interchange undone. Check correctness at n=32 and 128 and measure n=1024 wall time. Preserve full overwrite, read-only inputs, and the tolerance. Keep correctness-preserving follow-up or combined experiments open if they improve results.
children.subject: Loop interchange and OpenMP row parallelism

children.objective: Test whether multi-level blocking improves data reuse beyond the unblocked loop-interchange control. Vary row, column, and reduction block sizes and compare single-thread and budget-respecting parallel execution; measure any scratch or setup costs inside run. Validate all supplied sizes and tails against the required tolerance. Treat blocking as the primary hypothesis, not a ban on useful correctness-preserving combinations; retain controls that distinguish blocking’s contribution.
children.subject: Cache blocking and working-set reuse

children.objective: Test whether a register-blocked x86 SIMD microkernel and packed panels improve throughput. Use controlled unpacked/packed and kernel variants where practical to separate their contributions, and include packing cost in run-time measurements. Do not assume build flags or ISA support beyond what is safe for the frozen target. Validate tails and all supplied sizes against the tolerance, respect the thread budget, and retain slower correct components if they enable a faster later combination.
children.subject: Packed panels and SIMD microkernel

children.objective: First compare the unchanged scalar serial path with OpenMP work distribution using the `threads` budget, then compare row or tile scheduling (including static and bounded dynamic chunks) while keeping the per-pixel recurrence unchanged. Measure one- and four-core results and one-thread overhead; do not combine SIMD or row reuse before attributing the parallel effect. Validate exact counts and full output writes on n=1024, smaller checks, and shifted bounds. Later combinations remain valid experiments.
children.subject: Thread-budget-aware OpenMP work distribution

children.objective: Establish the scalar per-pixel baseline, then compare compiler-generated vectorization where viable under the frozen build with an explicit active-lane SIMD kernel. Start with one core to isolate per-core SIMD effects; report the four-core-budget result separately without adding a second threading strategy before attribution. Preserve coordinate and recurrence semantics and validate exact counts, tails, smaller checks, and shifted bounds. If vectorization is not viable or fails correctness, record that result rather than assuming ISA or compiler support; later combinations remain valid experiments.
children.subject: Exact SIMD evolution of adjacent pixels

children.objective: Compare against the scalar baseline and determine how many rows actually qualify for exact conjugate reuse before judging benefit. Derive pairing with low overhead, verify the generated float y coordinates are exact negatives, reuse counts only for verified pairs, and compute all other rows normally. Measure setup cost and net performance for pairable and asymmetric/shifted inputs supplied by the unchanged harness; do not assume symmetry or change the input protocol. Validate exact counts and full output writes; later combinations remain valid experiments.
children.subject: Runtime-verified conjugate row reuse

children.objective: Focus on reducing the hierarchical reduction’s work per launch and number of stages: explore multiple elements per thread or block, partial-sum layouts in scratch, and a complete device-side final stage. children.objective: Make intra-block reduction the main comparison: test a warp/shuffle method or permitted CUB BlockReduce against the current shared-memory tree, with matched block workload and end-to-end timings. The baseline’s 128-thread, one-element-per-thread configuration is a useful control, not a restriction; include a larger-work-per-block or hierarchical variant where useful to test interaction with T1 and whether the local improvement combines. Preserve exactness even if intermediate subsets can exceed int32, and validate tails and all required sizes.

children.objective: Compare staged partial-sum finalization with the alternative of explicitly zeroing output and atomically accumulating each block’s result. Include both launches in end-to-end timings; where possible, match the first-stage chunking and block reduction to a staged candidate so the finalization strategy is the contrast. Explore contention and chunk-size tradeoffs without assuming atomics win, and allow other correctness-preserving variants. Use unsigned modulo-2^32 or wider intermediates so cancellation cannot make intermediate signed overflow incorrect. Preserve stream ordering and buffer bounds; check n=0 only if the contract admits it.
children.subject: Finalisation atomique après initialisation explicite de la sortie

children.objective: Focus on the serial gk reduction, and explicitly compare a direct parallel reduction over B*L for each (h,j) that writes gk directly with a split reduction that writes current-call partials to scratch and then reduces them. Check whether the extra partial-write/read and final-kernel costs pay off in the complete call. Keep all scratch accesses within capacity for every valid shape, ensure every consumed partial is written, and assign fresh gk outputs. Preserve the exact zero-padding/indexing semantics, FP32 and required tolerance, ABI, and default stream. These are priority experiments, not restrictions on other correctness-preserving approaches.
children.subject: Contrast direct and split parallel reductions for gk

children.objective: Focus on improving forward and gx launch utilization. Compare row-oriented blocks with multirow or flattened contiguous-output tiles; consider a fused y/gx variant as a contrasting way to reduce duplicated launch/grid work. Account for the fact that flattening may cross rows or channels with different filter weights, and preserve exact indexing, masking, coalesced output writes where practical, fresh outputs, FP32, ABI, and default stream. Keep the implementation dimension-generic and compare complete-call timings. These are priority experiments, not restrictions on other correctness-preserving approaches.
children.subject: Contrast compact row, multirow, flat, and fused stencil mappings

children.objective: Dans src/candidate.py, développer un noyau Triton fusionné avec un CTA par ligne : réduction stable du maximum en FP32, exponentielle des valeurs décalées, réduction de la somme et écriture directe du résultat normalisé. Utiliser des masques et un choix de tuile génériques pour les largeurs de ligne, puis mesurer l’effet du nombre de warps et des paramètres de tuile, en priorisant la forme 4096x4096. Comparer également le chemin arithmétique FP32 standard à des variantes pertinentes d’exponentielle ou de normalisation (par exemple réciproque), sans supposer qu’elles sont plus rapides ou suffisamment précises. Ne conserver une variante que si elle satisfait toutes les vérifications de correction et la tolérance exigée. Préserver x, calculer à partir de l’entrée courante et comparer avec le même protocole officiel, allocations et lancements inclus.
children.subject: Softmax Triton fusionné par ligne : réglage du noyau et comparaison arithmétique

children.objective: Dans src/candidate.py, explorer une décomposition générique en plusieurs CTA par ligne pour les lignes longues. Une première étape calcule pour chaque segment son maximum et sa somme exponentielle décalée; une étape de sortie combine ces statistiques de façon stable, relit le segment d’entrée et écrit les probabilités normalisées. Mesurer les compromis du découpage, des statistiques temporaires, de l’allocation et des lancements supplémentaires face au noyau de référence et à la piste fusionnée. Préserver x, calculer à partir de l’entrée courante et valider toutes les formes et la tolérance; consigner aussi les cas où le surcoût rend cette méthode moins performante.
children.subject: Décomposition multi-CTA des lignes longues

children.objective: Isolate thread-level scaling in `src/candidate.cpp`: retain the baseline stencil expression and per-step arithmetic, and vary only the OpenMP work partition and team lifetime. Compare a serial one-thread path with a one-thread OpenMP path to expose overhead, then measure the requested four-thread budget with synchronization between dependent steps. Keep the CPU thread count within `threads`, preserve buffer parity and boundaries, and include full output initialization and official correctness checks in comparisons.
children.subject: OpenMP scaling with the stencil kernel held fixed

children.objective: Isolate per-step SIMD and address/load handling: compare the existing scalar kernel with a compiler-vectorizable x-inner loop while keeping the outer work partition identical. Measure at both requested thread budgets; if a threaded T1 implementation is used, label its combined result separately so its gain is not attributed to SIMD alone. Preserve all valid dimensions and the stated error bound, and report correctness and whole-call wall time including initialization.
children.subject: SIMD kernel comparison under a fixed outer schedule

children.objective: Focus on temporal reuse across the six dependent steps. Compare a spatial-only tiled control with multi-step temporal tiles, handling radius-three dependency halos, initialized boundaries, and buffer parity correctly. Keep any outer threading policy fixed rather than introducing a second scheduling search; measure the requested budgets and report threaded combinations as interactions, not as isolated tiling gains. Include full-call timing and official correctness checks.
children.subject: Temporal blocking versus spatial-only tiling

children.objective: Implement a one-pass fused scan using scalar, bounded loads: each CTA accumulates abs(x), performs a block reduction, and atomically adds its block total to output. Reset output before the kernel in the default stream. Explore CTA count and scalar grid-stride scheduling to assess occupancy and atomic contention; leave vectorized loads and load-width/coarsening experiments to T3. Do not rely on initialized scratch. Validate output overwrite and correctness at all required sizes, and compare repeatable full-call timings including reset and launch costs.
children.subject: Scalar fused sum(abs) with block-aggregate atomics

children.objective: Implement a fused scalar scan in which each CTA processes a tile and writes one partial sum to scratch, followed by a kernel that reduces exactly the current call’s partials and overwrites output. This avoids full-size scratch traffic and atomics, but retains two launches. Explore tile size and partial count for this architecture; do not add vectorized-load experiments. Ensure every consumed partial is written in the current call and tails are bounded. Validate all required sizes and compare full-call timings, including both launches.
children.subject: Fused scalar scan with scratch partials and a final reduction

children.objective: Isolate load format using a fused block-atomic sum(abs) implementation. Hold grid geometry, per-thread element mapping, accumulation scheme, block reduction, and output-reset behavior fixed between scalar and vectorized variants; compare only the load path. Use a correct scalar path for unsupported alignment and a bounded tail, without assuming input alignment. Validate all required sizes and retain vectorization only if repeated full-call timings improve without correctness regressions.
children.subject: Controlled scalar-versus-vectorized loads in a fused atomic scan

children.objective: Explore a single-core, whole-buffer x86 SIMD validator that checks UTF-8 lead/continuation relationships and restricted second-byte cases across blocks, including cross-block state, tails, overlong forms, surrogates, and values above U+10FFFF. Distinguish this from merely adding T2’s word-at-a-time ASCII scanner; SIMD handling of ASCII may still be part of the vector validator. Use only paths supported by the frozen build, with a correct fallback, and do not change compiler flags or inspect runtime environment. Preserve the run ABI and full-output behavior. Measure native wall time on the official n=65536 mixed-width input and verify ASCII and malformed/truncated cases, especially at block boundaries.
children.subject: Blockwise SIMD validation of UTF-8 structure

children.objective: Test whether bounded machine-word high-bit checks improve ASCII-run skipping in the official mixed-width input, rather than assuming that input is mostly ASCII. Keep the baseline scalar decoder for non-ASCII bytes initially to isolate this change. Use safe loads and tails without overreads or aliasing assumptions, and ensure no byte is skipped when a word contains a high bit. Preserve the run ABI, full-output behavior, and one-core budget. Measure under the official protocol; ASCII and malformed inputs are correctness checks, not proxies for mixed-width performance.
children.subject: Word-at-a-time ASCII-run scanning

children.objective: Explore replacing the branch-heavy scalar per-code-point loop with a compact scalar UTF-8 DFA or equivalent branch-light state machine. Ensure transitions reject illegal lead bytes, invalid continuations, overlong encodings, surrogates, and values above U+10FFFF, and ensure end-of-input is accepted only in the initial state. Preserve the run ABI, full-output behavior, and one-core budget. Compare official mixed-width wall time to baseline and verify ASCII and malformed/truncated correctness.
children.subject: Branch-light scalar UTF-8 state machine

children.objective: Paralléliser les pixels avec OpenMP en respectant threads comme budget maximal et en gardant le calcul de chaque pixel inchangé. Comparer le découpage statique par lignes à des plages contiguës de pixels et à une politique par blocs adaptée à une charge variable, en mesurant le compromis déséquilibre/coût d’ordonnancement. Préserver l’écriture complète de l’image et vérifier correction et temps à 1, 4 et 40 threads.
children.subject: Parallélisme et équilibrage du travail par pixels

children.objective: Optimiser le chemin scalaire de Density/D : réduire les clamps ou calculs d’adresse redondants tout en préservant le domaine, le comportement aux bords, les huit valeurs interpolées et l’ordre des Lerp. Garder les positions et pas d’échantillonnage du ray marcher inchangés ; ne pas introduire de chemin SIMD, pour isoler cette piste. Valider sur densité modifiée et résolution caméra mise à l’échelle, puis mesurer aux budgets de threads officiels.
children.subject: Coût du sampler scalaire d’interpolation trilinéaire

children.objective: Étudier le SIMD intra-thread sur des rayons de pixels indépendants comme contraste à l’OpenMP de T1. Comparer une voie vectorisée par lots au calcul scalaire, en conservant pour chaque voie la suite des positions, le nombre et l’ordre des échantillons, les sommes, les conditions d’arrêt et la transmittance d’ombre ; utiliser des masques pour les rayons inactifs ou de longueurs différentes. Garder Density/D scalaire intacte et, si nécessaire, ajouter un chemin vectorisé distinct. N’utiliser que des instructions prises en charge par la cible et le build figés, sans changer les options ni faire de détection runtime. Mesurer correction et performance aux budgets officiels, puis évaluer séparément l’intégration avec T1/T2.
children.subject: Vectorisation intra-thread des rayons de pixels
